NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VII: KNOWLEDGE, CONSENT AND SHARED WORK (LCG-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume III concepts (201-300): weather readers and navigators, seed keepers and terrace builders, permission and consent, who leads and who is heard, homes built by many hands, songs for the uncelebrated, and a village writing its own story.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: The apprentice cook keeps losing the beat of the fishers' welcome chant: teach them, or give them another job.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has made up a playful chant to greet the fishing crews when they come in, with the cooks banging pots in rhythm. It is wonderful, except that (friend), the newest apprentice cook, has no sense of rhythm at all, and bangs whenever (friend.he/she) feels like it. What should (subject) do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) practices with (friend) every day, tapping the rhythm on (friend.his/her) shoulder. (friend) gets slightly better. On the big day, (friend.he/she) bangs at all the wrong moments and the fishers laugh so hard they nearly drop the catch. They ask for it that way every time.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) asks (friend) to wave the welcome flag instead. (friend) waves it enormously, with total commitment, and becomes the most famous part of the welcome. The fishers wave back from far out at sea.
